collection.credit:
NEW EVENTS — PONDERING HOW LIFE HAS GONE (LIF-01..50, draft for the owner, 2026-11-15)
Adults of every age looking at their own lives so far: roads not taken, quiet satisfaction, small regrets, unexpected pride, things left unfinished, luck, gratitude and plenty of amusement. Nobody has to reach a verdict.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. Edit anything and send it back; nothing ships until you approve.

ledger.why: the casting line, carried out as the roles' ages (picks an elder and a young adult, 18-25)

collection.description: An elder watches a young adult they helped raise teach the little ones: say they are proud, or just watch.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: (subject) is watching (friend), a young adult, teaching a group of little ones how to throw a net. (subject) remembers when (friend) was one of those little ones, tangled up in (friend.his/her) own net, yelling. Over the years (subject) has helped raise a lot of the village's children, in small ways: a meal here, a scolding there, a story when they couldn't sleep.

o2.name: Outcome B
o2.text: (subject) just watches. The children are yelling and tangled, exactly as (friend) once was. (friend) is patient, mostly. (subject) can see bits of (subject.him/her)self in the way (friend) bends down to their level, and bits of other people too, and bits that are just (friend). (subject.He/she) doesn't say anything. (subject.He/she) doesn't need to. (subject.He/she) goes home feeling quietly enormous.

o1__fx.name: Outcome A
o1__fx.text: (subject) waits until the lesson's done and tells (friend) (friend.he/she) did well. (friend) is a bit embarrassed. "I learned it from you." (subject) shakes (subject.his/her) head. "You learned it from lots of people. I just gave you a few of the knots." (friend) grins. "You also yelled at me a lot." "You deserved it," says (subject). "You threw a net at a pig."
